### Observed differences

- Before, every trace contained A22 and each of A31, A32, A37 and A38 exactly once; in the later window each of these five activities appears in only about half of the traces (about 100 of 200), still exactly once when present and never repeated in either window. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- A20's successors changed completely: before, its outgoing transitions went to A31, A32, A37 and A38 in roughly equal shares (about 22–28 in 100 each); in the later window A20 leads almost always straight to A23 (about 995 in 1,000), and the A20-to-A23 distance fell from a fixed five steps to one step. [DIR001, LAG001]
- A21 previously always led to A22; in the later window about half of its outgoing transitions go to A22 and about half go into the block A31/A32/A37/A38 (about 10–18 in 100 per member). [DIR002]
- The block's exit changed: before, each block member led to A23 in about 22–29 in 100 of its outgoing transitions; in the later window A23 is practically gone as their successor (at most about 1 in 100) and A26 appears (about 18–28 in 100). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- A22 and the block became mutually exclusive: they co-occurred in every trace before (block before A22), but in only about 1 in 200 later traces; afterwards about half the traces contain A22 only and about half the block only. The block also swapped sides relative to A21 and A23: it always ran before them before, whereas in the later window A21 and A23 precede the block in the traces containing both. [REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020]
- The A21-to-A26 distance, previously always two steps, is now two steps in about half the traces (via A22) and five steps in the other half (via the block). [LAG006]
- Event positions moved accordingly: the block shifted from about 0.40 to about 0.58 of the trace, A23 from about 0.47 to about 0.38, A21 from about 0.61 to about 0.54 and A22 from about 0.64 to about 0.59, while A23 and A26 still occur in every trace in both windows. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009]
- Within the block, the four activities keep a mixed, unfixed mutual order in both windows. [REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030]
- The elapsed time between consecutive completions of A42 and A43 roughly doubled, from a mean of about 1.0 h to about 2.0 h (median about 1.0 h to about 2.0 h; 155 vs 162 intervals). [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the routing around the four-activity block A31, A32, A37, A38 changed: in the earlier window every case ran from A20 through the block (in mixed order) to A23, and later from A21 via A22 to A26, whereas in the later window A20 leads directly to A23 and the block instead runs after A21 as an alternative to A22, ending in A26 — so the block and A22 became mutually exclusive options, each taken in about half of the cases. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, REL007, REL013, REL017, REL021, LAG001, LAG006, OCC001, OCC002]

This goes far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces: the control-flow family yielded 60 qualifying items against roughly 0.62 expected by chance, each difference exceeding about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits, and the successor replacement at A20 and A21, the order flips around the block, the collapse of the A20-to-A23 distance and the halving of participation all describe the same re-routing while A23 and A26 remain universal. [DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, OCC001, POS004, POS005]

Limitations: the exact internal sequence of the block stays unresolved, a few post-change lag profiles for the block's old and new neighbours rest on a single observed pair, and about one trace in 200 in the later window still shows the old routing; the aggregate windows also cannot show whether the same kinds of cases changed route or whether the two windows capture a shifted mix of case types that always followed different routes. [REL025, LAG002, LAG007, DIR001]

Other differences: the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A42 and A43 roughly doubled (mean about 1.0 h to about 2.0 h, 155 vs 162 intervals) — a timing change in its own right with no structural counterpart in the evidence, since A42 and A43 appear in no other item. [TWAIT001]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 150 units tested, 0.63 items expected without change overall. By family:
- control_flow: 124 units tested, 60 items, 0.62 expected. So 60 items vs 0.62 expected — massively more than expected by chance. This is a huge signal.
- time: 26 units tested, 1 item, 0.013 expected. 1 item vs 0.013 expected — also more than expected, but 1 item is small; still, the control flow family has 60 items which is ~100x the expectation.

So the count is many orders of magnitude above the chance expectation for control flow. This is not "insufficient evidence" territory. Now I need to figure out what the behaviour change is.

Let me reconstruct the process from the evidence.

Activities mentioned: A20, A21, A22, A23, A26, A31, A32, A37, A38, A42, A43.

OCC items:
- OCC001 A22: before participation 1.0, after 0.5. Mean occurrences 1.0 → 0.5. So A22 occurred once in every trace before, in half the traces after.
- OCC002 A31: 1.0 → 0.505.
- OCC003 A32: 1.0 → 0.505.
- OCC004 A37: 1.0 → 0.505.
- OCC005 A38: 1.0 → 0.505.

So A22, A31, A32, A37, A38 all went from occurring in every trace (once) to occurring in about half the traces.

DIR items (outgoing transitions of source):
- DIR001 A20: before → A37 0.28, A31 0.22, A38 0.255, A32 0.245 (roughly uniform over 4 targets). After → A23 0.995, A31 0.005. So A20 now almost always leads to A23.
- DIR002 A21: before → A22 1.0. After → A22 0.5, A32 0.175, A38 0.115, A31 0.1, A37 0.11. So A21 now leads to A22 half the time and to the group A31/A32/A37/A38 the other half.
- DIR003 A31: before → A38 0.27, A37 0.205, A23 0.25, A32 0.275. After → A37 0.287, A32 0.257, A38 0.178, A26 0.277. So A31 no longer leads to A23; instead leads to A26.
- DIR004 A32: before → A23 0.245, A31 0.29, A38 0.25, A37 0.215. After → A38 0.287, A31 0.218, A26 0.257, A37 0.238. A23 gone, A26 appears.
- DIR005 A37: before → A31 0.295, A38 0.225, A32 0.195, A23 0.285. After → A32 0.188, A38 0.307, A26 0.218, A31 0.287. A23 gone, A26 appears.
- DIR006 A38: before → A32 0.285, A37 0.3, A23 0.22, A31 0.195. After → A23 0.0099, A26 0.238, A32 0.208, A37 0.257, A31 0.287. A23 nearly gone, A26 appears.

So the group {A31, A32, A37, A38} previously cycled among themselves and to A23; now they lead to A26 instead of A23.

POS items:
- POS001 A20: mean position 0.333 → 0.353 (slightly later).
- POS002 A21: 0.613 → 0.536 (earlier).
- POS003 A22: 0.641 → 0.593, support 1.0 → 0.5.
- POS004 A23: 0.473 → 0.384 (earlier).
- POS005 A26: 0.669 → 0.640 (slightly earlier).
- POS006 A31: 0.405 → 0.586 (much later), support 1.0 → 0.505.
- POS007 A32: 0.401 → 0.578 (later), support 0.505.
- POS008 A37: 0.402 → 0.580 (later), support 0.505.
- POS009 A38: 0.402 → 0.582 (later), support 0.505.

REL items: many. Let me summarise:
- REL001 (A20, A22): before co-occur always, A20 before A22 always. After: co-occur 0.5, A20-only 0.5, A20 before A22 0.5. So in half the traces A20 occurs without A22.
- REL002-005 (A20 with A31/A32/A37/A38): same pattern — before always co-occur with A20 first; after co-occur ~0.505, A20-only ~0.495.
- REL006 (A21, A22): before always co-occur, A21 before A22. After co-occur 0.5, A21-only 0.5.
- REL007-010 (A21 with A31/A32/A37/A38): before always co-occur with A21 AFTER the other (B_before_A = 1.0, i.e., A31 before A21). After: co-occur 0.505, A21-only 0.495, A21 before A31 0.5, B_before_A 0.005. So the order flipped: previously A31...A21, now A21...A31 in the traces where both occur.
